This petition has been filed to quash the FIR registered in Crime No.19 of 2021 on the file of the the first respondent police for the offences under Sections 498(A), 406, 506(1) of IPC, as against the petitioner.

2. The case of the prosecution is that the marriage between the petitioner and the second respondent was solemnized on 01.12.2014 and at the time of marriage, the petitioner's family demanded 100 sovereign of jewels and Rs.10 lakhs case and Rs.12,00,000/- worth car.
The petitioner was employed in Bosch at Bengaluru and after the marriage, they lived separately in a flat at Bengaluru.

The petitioner's family consulted an Astrolgist one Vetrivel at Delhi, who had stated that the petitioner's family is suffering from a black magic and in order to cure the same, the petitioner's family demanded Rs.2 lakhs from the second respondent.
Thereafter, the petitioner used to drink alcohol and beat the second respondent at the instance of his parents and relatives for getting property through the second respondent.
A counseling was arranged and after that the petitioner was silent and the second respondent was pregnant and stayed at her parent's house.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 3.
Thereafter, the petitioner's family informed the second respondent that if she get property from her family and then only she can live with the petitioner.

In the mean time, the second respondent with her child went along with the petitioner to Germany in view of his employment and the petitioner caused cruelty to the second respondent asking her to go and buy liquor and cigarette,
denying food to her and her child.
Therefore, she lodged complaint to the police in Germany and on the request of the petitioner, the same was withdrawn by the second respondent.
Thereafter, the petitioner brought the second respondent and her child to India and dropped them at the second respondent parent's house.
4. It is further alleged that the petitioner's family again demanded property and nabbed the child from her and refused to give the child.
Therefore, the second respondent lodged complaint before the All Women Police Station, Erode and domestic violence complaint in D.V.O.P.No.9 of 2021 before the Additional Mahalir Court, Erode.
On 16.04.2021, the second respondent's father died and as such she has no money to eke out her livelihood.

Therefore, the second respondent asked the p e t i t i o n e r t o r e t u r n b a c k 1 0 0 s o v e r e i g n j e w e l s , R s . 1 0 l a k h c a s h a n d https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis car worth Rs.12 lakhs, which were paid to him at the time of marriage.
But the petitioner threatened the second respondent and refused to return back the seethana articles and refused to give the child.
On receipt of the complaint, the first respondent registered the FIR in Crime No.19 of 2021 for the above offences.
5. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is the sole accused in the complaint lodged by the second respondent.
The petitioner got married the second respondent on 01.12.2014.

The parents of the second respondent suppressed that the second respondent has been suffering from incurable form of bi-polar mental disorder due to which she is expressing mania excitement and comes uncontrollable with unsound mind.
In fact, she cannot even taken care of herself without the help of others.
Someone is keeping on helping her.
The said fact was suppressed by her parents and got married.

5.2. He further submitted that after filing the domestic violence case, the second respondent lodged the present compliant.
The first respondent without even conducting any enquiry registered the FIR.
Now the divorce petition and the petition under Domestic Violence Act are pending.
In fact, in the domestic violence complaint, the second respondent filed petition for custody of the minor child.
The trial recorded the behavior of the second respondent and dismissed the petition.
The https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis trial Court concluded that the second respondent acted only because of her sufferings due to mental disorder viz., bi-polar disorder.

Therefore, she was denied the custody of the minor child in Crl.M.P.No.2572 of 2021 in D.V.C.No.9 of 2021 by the learned Judicial Magistrate, Additional Mahila Court, Erode, by an order dated 09.08.2012.

sentences.text: Therefore, the FIR has been foisted only to wreck vengeance as against the petitioner and the allegations are bald and vague.

5.3. In support his contention, he relied upon the judgment of this Court reported in 2020 SCC Online Mad 23745 in the case of Arunkumar Vs. State as follows :-
26.

In the above cases, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India held that the word "cruelty" has envisage under Section 498A of IPC there must be such a conduct on the part of the husband or relatives of the husband of woman which is of such a nature as to cause the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health whether mental or physical of the woman.
27. In the case on hand, there is no such allegations in the FIR as well as the statement of the witnesses.
The ingredients to constitute the offence https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis under explanation A of 498 of IPC are not at all mentioned in the FIR and also in the statement of the witnesses.
When the absence there of, no offence is made out under Section 498A of IPC as against the petitioner.

Insofar as the offence under Section 406 of IPC is concerned the allegation made in the FIR as well as the statements do not satisfy the definition of the criminal breach of trust as contained in Section 405 of IPC.

It is relevant to extract the offence under Sections 405 of IPC as follows :-

Criminal breach of trust

Whoever, being in any manner entrusted with property, or with any dominion over property, dishonestly misappropriates or converts to his own use that property, or dishonestly uses or disposes of that property in violation of any direction of law prescribing the mode in which such trust is to be discharged, or of any legal contract, express or implied, which he has made touching the discharge of such trust, or wilfully suffers any other person so to do, commits "criminal breach of trust".
406. Punishment for criminal breach of trust  Whoever commits criminal breach of trust shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both."
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 6.
Heard the learned counsel appearing on either side and perused the material placed before this Court.
7. On perusal of FIR revealed that there are so many allegations made as against the petitioner.

Though the petitioner stated that the second respondent is suffering from bi-polar mental disorder and as such she used to express mania excitement, to prove the same, he did not even produce any medical records.

Further, according to the petitioner, while getting down in the Bangaluru airport,
the second respondent was running in the airport runway without any dress.
If at all the second respondent naked and run around in the airport runway, the airport authority had caused nuisance case and as such they would have taken action as against the second respondent.
Though the petitioner alleged so many allegations in the divorce petition, in order to prove the same, he never produced any evidence.
8. That apart, the allegations made against the petitioner are serious in nature and therefore, it has to be investigated in depth.
Further, the allegations leveled as against the petitioner clearly constitute the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis offence under Sections 498(A), 406, 506(1) of IPC.
Though, the petition for custody of the child was dismissed, it doesn't mean that the allegations made against the petitioner are false.
Further, the FIR is not an encyclopedia and it need not contain all facts and it cannot be quashed in the threshold.
This Court finds that the FIR discloses prima facie commission of cognizable offence and as such this Court cannot interfere with the investigation.
The investigating machinery has to step in to investigate, grab and unearth the crime in accordance with the procedures prescribed in the Code.

9. In this regard, it is relevant to rely upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India passed in Crl.A.No.255 of 2019 dated 12.02.2019 in the case of Sau. Kamal Shivaji Pokarnekar vs.
the State of Maharashtra & ors., as follows:-
"4.

sentences.text: The only point that arises for our consideration in this case is whether the High Court was right in setting aside the order by which process was issued.
It is settled law that the Magistrate, at the stage of taking cognizance and summoning, is required Praveen vs The State Rep.

By on 17 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56304824/
4 to apply his judicial mind only with a view to taking cognizance of the offence, or in o t h e r w o r d s , t o f i n d o u t w h e t h e r a p r i m a f a c i e c a s e h a s https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis been made out for summoning the accused persons.

The learned Magistrate is not required to evaluate the merits of the material or evidence in support of the complaint, because the Magistrate must not undertake the exercise to find out whether the materials would lead to a conviction or not.
5. Quashing the criminal proceedings is called for only in a case where the complaint does not disclose any offence, or is frivolous, vexatious, or oppressive.
If the allegations set out in the complaint do not constitute the offence of which cognizance has been taken by the Magistrate, it is open to the High Court to quash the same.
It is not necessary that a meticulous analysis of the case should be done before the Trial to find out whether the case would end in conviction or acquittal.
If it appears on a reading of the complaint and consideration of the allegations therein, in the light of the statement made on oath that the ingredients of the offence are disclosed
, there would be no justification for the High Court to interfere.

9. Having heard the learned Senior Counsel and examined the material on record, we are of the considered view that the High Court ought not to have set aside the order passed by the Trial Court issuing summons to the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Respondents.
A perusal of the complaint discloses that prima facie, offences that are alleged against the Respondents.
The correctness or otherwise of the said allegations has to be decided only in the Trial.
At the initial stage of issuance of process it is not open to the Courts to stifle the proceedings by entering into the merits of the contentions made on behalf of the accused.
Criminal complaints cannot be quashed only on the ground that the allegations made therein appear to be of a civil nature.
If the ingredients of the offence alleged against the accused are prima facie made out in the complaint, the criminal proceeding shall not be interdicted."
10. In view of the above discussions, this Court is not inclined to quash the First Information Report.
Accordingly, this Criminal Original Petition stands dismissed.

However, considering the facts and circumstances, the first respondent is directed to complete the investigation in Crime No.19 of 2021 and file a final report within a period of twelve weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this Order,
before the jurisdiction Magistrate, if not already filed.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petitions are closed.
